purpose: This medicine is used to treat serious, life-threatening fungal infections in your body. It is often used when other antifungal medicines have not worked or caused too many side effects. Doctors also use it to prevent fungal infections in people with weakened immune systems, such as those going through bone marrow transplants.
how_it_works: This medicine works by attacking and destroying the outer wall of fungal cells, which kills the fungus. Think of it like poking holes in the fungus until it falls apart. The 'liposome' part means the medicine is wrapped in a tiny fat bubble, which helps it get to the right places in your body more safely and with fewer side effects than older versions of this drug.
common_side_effects: Fever, chills, or shaking — especially during the IV infusion. Nausea, vomiting, or stomach upset. Headache or back pain. Low potassium or magnesium levels in your blood. Swelling or redness at the IV site. Feeling tired or weak.
warnings: This medicine can affect your kidneys, so your doctor will regularly check your kidney function with blood tests. It can cause low levels of important minerals like potassium and magnesium, which can affect your heart. Tell your doctor right away if you have trouble breathing, chest pain, or a severe reaction during your infusion. Let your doctor know about all other medicines you take, as many drugs can interact with this one.
typical_dosing: This medicine is given through an IV (directly into a vein) by a nurse or doctor, usually once a day. The dose depends on your weight, the type of infection, and your overall health. Infusions typically take about 2 hours. Your healthcare team will decide the exact dose and how long you need treatment.
